'''CMS''' is an international [[law firm]] that offers [[Legal advice|legal]] and [[Tax advice|tax advisory]] services. CMS coordinates the activities of its members through CMS Legal Services EEIG, a [[european economic interest grouping]].<ref name="unternehmensregister.de">{{Cite web|url=https://www.unternehmensregister.de/|title=CMS Legal Services|website=Unternehmensregister|publisher=Bundesanzeiger Verlag|date=2001-07-06|access-date=2019-03-01|language=de}}</ref> It consists of 18 independent law firms, with about 80 offices worldwide.

== History ==
In 1999, six [[Europe]]an law firms with 1,400+ lawyers and roughly [[Deutsche Mark|DM]] 500 million in joint revenues came together to form CMS.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Wirtschaftskanzleien fusionieren.|newspaper=Hamburger Abendblatt|date=1999-04-30|language=de|page=21}}</ref> The CMS brand combined the names of two founding law firms, Cameron McKenna (UK) and Hasche Sigle (Germany).<ref>{{Cite web |title=FAQs |url=https://cms.law/en/aut/cms-job-opportunities/applications/faqs |access-date=2025-10-14 |website=cms.law |language=en}}</ref> Under the CMS brand, which initially drew criticism,<ref>{{Cite news|first1=Claudia|last1=Tödtmann|title=Anwälte: Versteckspielen gilt nicht.|newspaper=Wirtschaftswoche|date=1999-09-09|language=de|page=120}}</ref> a "partnership of partnerships" emerged.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Neue Vereinigung von Anwälten|newspaper=Börsen-Zeitung|date=1999-05-04|language=de|page=26}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|first1=Alexander|last1=Pfeffer|title=Europäische Union der Anwälte|newspaper=WirtschaftsBlatt|date=1999-06-22|language=de|page=6}}</ref> The member law firms retained their established names.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thelawyer.com/issues/19-november-2007/integration-push-sparks-cms-name-dropping-row/|title=Integration Push Sparks CMS Name-Dropping Row|website=The Lawyer|date=2007-11-19|access-date=2019-03-11|language=en}}</ref>

Initially, CMS included law firms from Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, and the United Kingdom, among others.<ref>{{Cite news|title=Sechs europäische Spitzen-Kanzleien arbeiten zusammen.|newspaper=Die Welt|date=1999-04-29|language=de|page=2}}</ref> Over the course of the 2000s, additional law firms joined from other countries.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.thelawyer.com/issues/12-february-2001/francis-lefebvre-joins-the-cms-global-alliance/|title=Francis Lefebvre Joins the CMS Global Alliance|website=The Lawyer|date=2001-02-12|access-date=2019-03-11|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|first1=Vera|last1=Wicke|url=https://www.juve.de/nachrichten/namenundnachrichten/2002/03/cms-steuert-nach-italien|title=CMS steuert nach Italien|publisher=Juve Verlag|date=2002-03-01|access-date=2019-03-11|language=de}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|first1=Anna|last1=Ward|url=https://www.law.com/legal-week/2017/07/10/cms-moves-into-monaco-market-via-tie-up-with-local-firm/|title=CMS Moves into Monaco Market via Tie-Up with Local Firm|website=Legalweek|date=2017-07-10|access-date=2019-03-11|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|first1=Beat|last1=Brenner|title=Schweizerisch-britische Anwaltsfusion: Erlach Klainguti Stettler Wille zieht es nach London.|newspaper=Neue Zürcher Zeitung|date=2000-05-15|language=de|page=20}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|first1=Christine|last1=Albert|url=https://www.juve.de/nachrichten/namenundnachrichten/2004/11/nun-auch-in-spanien-cms-erweitert-netzwerk|title=Nun auch in Spanien: CMS erweitert Netzwerk.|publisher=Juve Verlag|date=2004-11-04|access-date=2019-03-11|language=de}}</ref>

In 2008, the law firm opened its first joint office in Russia.<ref>{{Cite news|first1=Walther|last1=Becker|title=CMS-Kanzleien in Moskau zusammen|newspaper=Börsen-Zeitung|date=2008-12-03|language=de|page=10}}</ref> It merged with [[Nabarro LLP|Nabarro]] and [[Olswang]] in 2016.<ref>{{Cite news|first1=John|last1=Hyde|url=https://www.lawgazette.co.uk/practice/its-a-deal-cms-confirms-merger-with-olswang-and-nabarro/5058217.article|title=It's a Deal: CMS Confirms Merger with Olswang and Nabarro|website=The Law Society Gazette|date=2016-10-10|access-date=2019-03-11|language=en}}</ref>

CMS is part of the Society of Media Lawyers, an industry group of law firms that specialize in libel lawsuits and which lobbied against anti-[[Strategic lawsuit against public participation|SLAPP]] ( Strategic lawsuit against public participation) legislation.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Libel lawyers cast clients as underdogs in bid to halt anti-SLAPP law |url=https://www.thebureauinvestigates.com/stories/2026-05-14/a-list-libel-lawyers-cast-clients-as-underdogs-in-bid-to-halt-anti-slapp-law |access-date=2026-05-16 |website=TBIJ |language=en}}</ref>

=== Russia ===
CMS was involved in legal action against ''Financial Times'' journalist [[Catherine Belton]] and her publisher HarperCollins over her book ''[[Putin's People: How the KGB Took Back Russia and Then Took On the West|Putin's People]]''.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2022-04-19 |title=US congressman urges Biden to ban six UK lawyers for 'enabling' oligarchs |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2022/apr/19/us-congressman-urges-biden-to-ban-six-uk-lawyers-for-enabling-oligarchs |access-date=2022-05-04 |website=the Guardian |language=en}}</ref>

In April 2022, CMS law firm was named alongside [[Harbour Litigation Funding]] by [[Kevin Hollinrake]] MP, in a letter to the Chancellor of the Exchequer [[Rishi Sunak]] MP, as two professional services firms acting for the benefit of Russian state entities during the invasion of Ukraine. The letter highlighted that both Harbour and CMS are working on behalf of the Russian state-owned [[Deposit Insurance Agency of Russia|DIA]] to bypass sanction regimes and obtain funds and assets from abroad in order to fund the [[Russian invasion of Ukraine|invasion of Ukraine]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2022-04-11 |title=Tory backbencher calls on government to close 'loopholes' letting London firms work for the Kremlin |url=https://www.cityam.com/tory-backbencher-calls-on-government-to-close-loopholes-letting-london-firms-work-for-the-kremlin/ |access-date=2022-04-12 |website=CityAM |language=en-GB}}</ref>

CMS was named by U.S. congressman Steve Cohen as doing "unscrupulous" work for Russia that undermined democratic values and strengthened the Vladimir Putin regime in Russia. CMS rejected allegations of impropriety and said the firm had not accepted new instructions from individuals associated with the Putin regime.<ref name=":0" />
